goodreads: When the user has read and highly rated sequential volumes of a specific series and the candidate is the next sequential volume in that same series, strongly prefer it.

When a candidate belongs to a franchise the user has shown strong positive engagement with (e.g., read multiple volumes at 5 stars), prefer it over unrelated candidates even if the specific volume was not read.
Do not assume a highly-rated popular standalone classic is preferred merely due to high average rating; the user's own history and series continuity outweigh global popularity.
When the user's history contains mostly one format (e.g., manga, superhero, memoir) and a candidate matches that format/theme while others do not, prefer the matching candidate.
If a candidate is a later volume in a series but the user has not read earlier volumes in that series, do not treat it as a continuation preference.
Treat unreviewed/zero-rated read entries as weak signals of preference; rely more on explicit positive ratings for preference inference.
ml-1m: When a user's history is dominated by high ratings for classic/prestige drama, war, or crime films, prefer candidates in those genres over broad family/animation/musical titles.

When a user's history consists mostly of children's, animation, or family films, prefer those candidates; otherwise avoid animation/children's options unless the user's history shows positive ratings for them.
When a user's history shows low ratings for horror or thriller titles, deprioritize horror and thriller candidates unless they also match genres the user rated highly.
When a user's history shows strong positive ratings for romance or relationship dramas, prefer drama/romance candidates over action, horror, or children's options.
When a user's history shows strong positive ratings for comedy, prefer comedy candidates (including comedy-drama) over unrelated drama or horror options.
When a user's history shows strong positive ratings for action, sci-fi, or adventure, prefer those candidates over romance or children's titles, especially if recent ratings in those genres are high.
mobilerec: Prefer candidates in a category the user has rated positively (4-5 stars) at least once, especially games in action, casual, puzzle, word, card, role playing, or simulation, over categories absent from their history.

When a user's positive ratings are concentrated in games, prefer free game candidates (puzzle, casual, action, role playing, simulation) over non-game utility, finance, shopping, or productivity apps, even when those apps have very high review counts.

Avoid finance, banking, insurance, and business candidates unless the user has positively rated an app in a finance or business category; such candidates are rarely fits for game- or utility-focused users.
Avoid dating, casino, and social/video candidates when the user's history has no positive ratings in those categories, as these rarely match observed preferences.
When the user has positively rated productivity or utility tools (scanners, editors, tools), prefer free, high-review productivity/tools candidates over paid niche or unrelated-category options.
Among candidates matching a positively rated category, prefer the one with free price and a strong average rating and review volume over paid or low-review alternatives.
